The leaf shows dark, sooty black patches and spots scattered across the surface, with a grimy, dusty black coating in places. The leaf is otherwise green with no necrotic margins or powdery white bloom. This pattern — dark, soot-like deposits unevenly distributed on the leaf surface — is characteristic of Sooty Mould, caused by fungal growth on honeydew secretions from insects.

- No sunken lesions or water-soaked spots (rules out Anthracnose)
- No stem dieback or tip necrosis (rules out Die_Back)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- Black, sooty deposits on leaf surface = Sooty Mould
